artist.name: Mokita
artist.place_of_origin: Virginia, United States (early upbringing); western North Carolina (adolescence); Nashville, Tennessee (based)
artist.short_description: Nashville-based singer-songwriter and producer John-Luke Carter, whose Mokita project blends vulnerable pop writing with electronic and acoustic elements.
artist.biography: Mokita is the artist project of John-Luke Carter, an American singer-songwriter and producer based in Nashville, Tennessee. According to a 2026 profile by his distributor, Carter was originally from Virginia and moved to North Carolina as a teenager. He described growing up with classical piano training, teaching himself guitar, and turning toward production after moving to Nashville to write songs. Alongside his solo music, he has worked behind the scenes as a songwriter and producer for other performers. Early Mokita releases leaned toward electronic pop, but later material has made room for acoustic instruments and a more restrained presentation. 'Love Alone' arrived in 2018, and Carter explained in a contemporary interview that it was motivated by the fear of being vulnerable in a relationship. The 2019 song 'colorblind' drew attention for addressing depression and the challenge of communicating an internal experience to someone else. Later projects include the 2022 EP 'Color Me In,' a self-titled 2025 album, and the 2026 single 'easy come, easy go.' His distributor characterized the later single as concerned with timing and emotional clarity. On Afterglow, Mokita offers a route from confessional songwriting into understated electronic pop. Those cross-genre recommendations are editorial choices rather than claims made by Carter himself.
